children: , the world's largest contract chipmaker, is building a testing and training hub at a new industrial park in Kaohsiung. Its U.S. shares fell about 1.0% to $442.29 at 10.17am ET time on Thursday morning.

The two planned buildings are meant to help suppliers test packaging equipment and materials alongside TSMC's engineers. Operations are expected to start in the fourth quarter of 2029. A TSMC executive estimated that the setup could improve validation efficiency by 25% to 50%. That is a useful target, but it says nothing yet about how many more chips TSMC can package.

At $442.29, the shares stood 21.6% above the $363.73 GF Value shown in the graphic. That gap puts a sharper question behind the park announcement: how much faster can TSMC turn promising packaging tools into approved production processes? The company has given investors an efficiency estimate, but no investment figure, added capacity or customer commitments for this project.

title: TSMC Slips 1% as Packaging Moves Toward Supplier Validation
